summary: A skill can carry the instructions of one process switch value in `references/switch-<switch>-<value>.md`. `task_inputs.py` binds such a file as a required read only when the project's approved Process Policy sets that switch to that value, and otherwise neither reads nor hashes it, so a switch at its default leaves every manifest byte-identical, which a golden run on a fixture package proves. When the policy exists it is a project input of the manifest, and a draft or invalid policy fails the derivation. `templates/task-input-contract.md` states the rule and how an entry reads a switch before the flow step that names it. `tools/validate.py` rejects a switch reference for an undeclared switch or value or for the default value, one that no owning flow names, and a SKILL.md that links one. A switch reference binds only for a task whose entry runs one of the switch's owning flows, so an analysis challenger or an Experience reviewer, whose flows own no review switch, binds none of them; a switch whose registry entry declares `reference_scope: owning_flows` binds its references for every task of those flows, whichever skills the task selects.
